newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CLINTON SALUTES NHL'S STANLEY CUP CHAMPIONS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CLINTON SALUTES NHL'S STANLEY CUP CHAMPIONS.

text.p: President Bill Clinton rolled out the red carpet on Friday for the Colorado Avalanche, pro hockey's 1996 Stanley Cup champions, saying their teamwork was something for his Cabinet to emulate.

The Avalanche, led by star forward Joe Sakic and goalie Patrick Roy, beat the Florida Panthers in triple overtime in the final game of the championship playoffs last June in what Clinton called "a very awe-inspiring performance."

The Stanley Cup, the National Hockey League's most coveted prize, gleamed next to the podium in the White House East Room during a brief ceremony honouring the team, which was known as the Quebec Nordiques before moving to Colorado 18 months ago.
Clinton said the Avalanche's clutch performance "showed what teamwork is all about," and joked that he might "show those final minutes (of the last game) to the Cabinet over and over again."

Sakic, named Most Valuable Player in the playoff series, gave the president a team jersey emblazoned with the name Clinton across the back and the number 96. "We both had a great year," quipped the team captain, on crutches due to a recent calf injury.

NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman noted that Clinton, an avid basketball and football fan, had also been friendly to hockey during his first term. In Clinton's second term, Bettman joked, "Maybe we can even get you suited up and on the ice."
